exposure.needed: whether cert-manager signs with RSA keys of 3072 or 4096 bits (e.g. CA or self-signed issuer keys held in Secrets)

consequence.statement: Signatures made with 3072-bit RSA keys now use SHA-384 and those made with 4096-bit RSA keys now use SHA-512 instead of SHA-256. The release notes expect minimal impact, but operators using larger RSA keys should be aware of the change.
consequence.remediation: If you sign with 3072-bit or 4096-bit RSA keys, check that the systems relying on these certificates accept SHA-384 or SHA-512 signatures.

assertion.statement: In v1.17.0, cert-manager stops always using SHA-256 when signing with RSA and picks the hash from the RSA key length: SHA-384 for 3072-bit keys and SHA-512 for 4096-bit keys.
